metadata.title: Work-in-Progress: Implementing and Evaluating a Competency-Oriented Assessment in an Innovative Application-Oriented Course of Mechanical Engineering

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This work-in-progress paper describes a competency-oriented assessment design for a mechanical engineering course and plans evaluation using Teaching Analysis Poll (TAP) and questionnaires. It does not use an ILSA micro-dataset (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC) with sampling weights or plausible values; therefore, survey-weight variables are not part of the analysis pipeline. The study’s quantitative component is a cross-sectional questionnaire administered to students after course assessments, and the qualitative component is based on voluntary TAP participation with anonymous student voting. For any future large-scale implementation, weighting would only be relevant if the authors used a probability-based sampling design and analyzed results to make population-representative inferences; this is not described here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the study does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes from an ILSA assessment (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC) that are typically scaled using PVs. Instead, it evaluates a higher-education course assessment approach using TAP and student questionnaires about perceived competence and professional preparation. Missing-data handling is not reported because the paper is a work-in-progress design description and does not provide an empirical dataset with documented missingness procedures.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No ILSA micro-data are used. The paper describes a mechanical engineering course for advanced students with a planned evaluation at the end of the semester using TAP (voluntary participation for lecturers and students) and two cross-sectional questionnaires administered after the written assessment and after the group presentation. The paper does not report the final analytic sample size, nor any explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond course participation and voluntary TAP participation.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Literature synthesis outcome (not student-level prediction), finding that This work-in-progress paper presents a competency-oriented assessment design for an advanced mechanical engineering course, evaluated through Teaching Analysis Poll (TAP) and student questionnaires. The assessment consists of a written test (30%) and a group presentation of practical results (70%), with grading based on weighted scoring of requirements aligned to intended competencies. The authors report prior evidence from earlier course evaluations (e.g., self-estimated ability shifts from low to high after the course) and anticipate that the new evaluation will show higher subjective competence gains and a stronger increase in “scientific self-image and professionalism.” No ILSA program/cycle, achievement domain, or PV-based outcome is used; therefore, no PV handling or ML predictive performance metrics are applicable. The paper does not provide final end-of-semester questionnaire results yet (planned for August), and it does not document missing-data procedures, limiting the strength of any conclusions. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a design-and-evaluation plan for a higher-education course assessment (work-in-progress) rather than an empirical large-scale assessment or an ML predictive study. As a result, there is no ILSA dataset, no PV-based achievement outcome, no ML model training, and no reported predictive metrics. The paper also does not provide a final analytic sample size or country-level breakdown, because the evaluation results are anticipated rather than fully reported.
